verses.original: οὖν τρεῖς ἡμέρας μετὰ ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχείᾳ Φῆστος ἀνέβη ἀπὸ Καισαρείας εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα
verses.transliteration: oun treis hēmeras meta epibas tē eparcheia Phēstos anebē apo Kaisareias eis Hierosolyma
verses.literal: - Three days after his arrival in the province Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem

verses.original: τε οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ τῶν Ἰουδαίων πρῶτοι ἐνεφάνισάν αὐτῷ κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: te hoi archiereis kai hoi tōn Ioudaiōn prōtoi enephanisan autō kata tou Paulou kai parekaloun auton
verses.literal: [where] the chief priests and - vvv Jewish leaders presented their case . . . against - Paul They urged [Festus]

verses.original: αἰτούμενοι χάριν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως μεταπέμψηται αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ ποιοῦντες ἐνέδραν ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν
verses.transliteration: aitoumenoi charin kat’ autou hopōs metapempsētai auton eis Ierousalēm poiountes enedran anelein auton kata tēn hodon
verses.literal: to grant them a concession against [Paul] by summoning him to Jerusalem [ because ] they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way

verses.original: οὖν μὲν Ὁ Φῆστος ἀπεκρίθη τὸν Παῦλον τηρεῖσθαι εἰς Καισάρειαν δὲ ἑαυτὸν μέλλειν ἐκπορεύεσθαι ἐν τάχει
verses.transliteration: oun men Ho Phēstos apekrithē ton Paulon tēreisthai eis Kaisareian de heauton mellein ekporeuesthai en tachei
verses.literal: But - - Festus replied - Paul is being held in Caesarea and [I myself] am going there vvv soon

verses.original: φησίν οὖν εἴ ἐν τῷ ἀνδρὶ ἐστιν τί ἄτοπον Οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν Δυνατοὶ συνκαταβάντες κατηγορείτωσαν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: phēsin oun ei en tō andri estin ti atopon Hoi en hymin Dynatoi synkatabantes katēgoreitōsan autou
verses.literal: - So if - [this] man has done anything wrong {let} some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him [there]

verses.original: δὲ Διατρίψας οὐ πλείους ὀκτὼ ἢ δέκα ἡμέρας ἐν αὐτοῖς καταβὰς εἰς Καισάρειαν τῇ ἐπαύριον καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσεν τὸν Παῦλον ἀχθῆναι
verses.transliteration: de Diatripsas ou pleious oktō ē deka hēmeras en autois katabas eis Kaisareian tē epaurion kathisas epi tou bēmatos ekeleusen ton Paulon achthēnai
verses.literal: [After] spending no more than eight or ten days with them [Festus] went down to Caesarea The next day he sat on the judgment seat [and] ordered that - Paul be brought in

verses.original: δὲ αὐτοῦ παραγενομένου οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καταβεβηκότες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων περιέστησαν αὐτὸν καταφέροντες πολλὰ καὶ βαρέα αἰτιώματα ἃ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀποδεῖξαι
verses.transliteration: de autou paragenomenou hoi Ioudaioi katabebēkotes apo Hierosolymōn periestēsan auton katapherontes polla kai barea aitiōmata ha ouk ischyon apodeixai
verses.literal: [When] [Paul] arrived the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him bringing many - serious charges that vvv they could not prove

verses.original: Τοῦ Παύλου ἀπολογουμένου ὅτι ἥμαρτον τι Οὔτε εἰς τὸν νόμον τῶν Ἰουδαίων οὔτε εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν οὔτε εἰς Καίσαρά
verses.transliteration: Tou Paulou apologoumenou hoti hēmarton ti Oute eis ton nomon tōn Ioudaiōn oute eis to hieron oute eis Kaisara
verses.literal: [Then] Paul made his defense - I have committed no offense . . . . . . against the law of the Jews [or] against the temple [or] against Caesar

verses.original: δὲ Ὁ Φῆστος θέλων καταθέσθαι χάριν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Παύλῳ Θέλεις ἀναβὰς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα κριθῆναι ἐπ’ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων
verses.transliteration: de Ho Phēstos thelōn katathesthai charin tois Ioudaiois apokritheis eipen tō Paulō Theleis anabas eis Hierosolyma krithēnai ep’ emou ekei peri toutōn
verses.literal: But - Festus wishing to do the Jews a favor . . . . . . . . . - said - to Paul Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me - on these [charges]

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Παῦλος Εἶπεν εἰμι Ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος Καίσαρος οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι ἠδίκησα οὐδὲν Ἰουδαίους ὡς σὺ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκεις κάλλιον
verses.transliteration: de ho Paulos Eipen eimi Hestōs epi tou bēmatos Kaisaros hou me dei krinesthai ēdikēsa ouden Ioudaious hōs sy kai epiginōskeis kallion
verses.literal: - - Paul replied I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar where I ought to be tried I have done nothing wrong . . . to [the] Jews as you [yourself] know very well

verses.original: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἀδικῶ καὶ πέπραχά τι ἄξιον θανάτου οὐ παραιτοῦμαι τὸ ἀποθανεῖν δὲ εἰ ἐστιν οὐδέν ὧν οὗτοι κατηγοροῦσίν μου οὐδείς δύναται χαρίσασθαι με αὐτοῖς ἐπικαλοῦμαι Καίσαρα
verses.transliteration: ei men oun adikō kai pepracha ti axion thanatou ou paraitoumai to apothanein de ei estin ouden hōn houtoi katēgorousin mou oudeis dynatai charisasthai me autois epikaloumai Kaisara
verses.literal: If however . . . I am guilty - [of] anything worthy of death vvv I do not refuse - to die But if there is no [truth] to their accusations against me no one has the right to hand me over . . . to them I appeal to Caesar

verses.original: Τότε ὁ Φῆστος συλλαλήσας μετὰ τοῦ συμβουλίου ἀπεκρίθη ἐπικέκλησαι Καίσαρα ἐπὶ Καίσαρα πορεύσῃ
verses.transliteration: Tote ho Phēstos syllalēsas meta tou symbouliou apekrithē epikeklēsai Kaisara epi Kaisara poreusē
verses.literal: Then - Festus conferred with [his] council [and] replied You have appealed to Caesar To Caesar you will go

verses.original: δὲ τινῶν Ἡμερῶν διαγενομένων ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἀγρίππας καὶ Βερνίκη κατήντησαν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀσπασάμενοι τὸν Φῆστον
verses.transliteration: de tinōn Hēmerōn diagenomenōn ho basileus Agrippas kai Bernikē katēntēsan eis Kaisareian aspasamenoi ton Phēston
verses.literal: [After] several days had passed - King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects - to Festus

verses.original: δὲ ὡς διέτριβον ἐκεῖ πλείους ἡμέρας ὁ Φῆστος ἀνέθετο τὰ κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον τῷ βασιλεῖ λέγων ἐστιν τίς Ἀνήρ ὑπὸ Φήλικος καταλελειμμένος δέσμιος
verses.transliteration: de hōs dietribon ekei pleious hēmeras ho Phēstos anetheto ta kata ton Paulon tō basilei legōn estin tis Anēr hypo Phēlikos kataleleimmenos desmios
verses.literal: Since . . . they were staying . . . several days - Festus laid out vvv vvv vvv Paul’s case before the king - There is a certain man [whom] Felix left in prison

verses.original: μου γενομένου εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐνεφάνισαν περὶ οὗ αἰτούμενοι καταδίκην κατ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: mou genomenou eis Hierosolyma hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi tōn Ioudaiōn enephanisan peri hou aitoumenoi katadikēn kat’ autou
verses.literal: While I was in Jerusalem the chief priests and - elders of the Jews presented their case . . . . . . [and] requested a judgment against him

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθην πρὸς οὓς ὅτι ἔστιν οὐκ ἔθος Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ἄνθρωπον πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορούμενος ἔχοι λάβοι τόπον κατὰ πρόσωπον τοὺς κατηγόρους τε ἀπολογίας περὶ τοῦ ἐγκλήματος
verses.transliteration: apekrithēn pros hous hoti estin ouk ethos Rhōmaiois charizesthai tina anthrōpon prin ē ho katēgoroumenos echoi laboi topon kata prosōpon tous katēgorous te apologias peri tou enklēmatos
verses.literal: I told - [them] that it is not [the] Roman custom . . . to hand a man {over} before - [he] . . . - has had [an] opportunity to face [his] accusers and defend himself against [their] charges

verses.original: οὖν αὐτῶν Συνελθόντων ἐνθάδε ποιησάμενος μηδεμίαν ἀναβολὴν τῇ ἑξῆς καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσα τὸν ἄνδρα ἀχθῆναι
verses.transliteration: oun autōn Synelthontōn enthade poiēsamenos mēdemian anabolēn tē hexēs kathisas epi tou bēmatos ekeleusa ton andra achthēnai
verses.literal: So [when] they came here {with me} I did not delay The next [day] I sat on the judgment seat [and] ordered that the man be brought in

verses.original: περὶ οὗ οἱ κατήγοροι σταθέντες ἔφερον οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν πονηρῶν ὧν ἐγὼ ὑπενόουν
verses.transliteration: peri hou hoi katēgoroi stathentes epheron oudemian aitian ponērōn hōn egō hypenooun
verses.literal: vvv [But when his] - accusers rose to speak vvv vvv they did not charge [him] with [any of the] crimes - I had expected

verses.original: δέ εἶχον τινα ζητήματα πρὸς αὐτὸν περὶ τῆς ἰδίας δεισιδαιμονίας καὶ περί τινος Ἰησοῦ τεθνηκότος ὃν ὁ Παῦλος ἔφασκεν ζῆν
verses.transliteration: de eichon tina zētēmata pros auton peri tēs idias deisidaimonias kai peri tinos Iēsou tethnēkotos hon ho Paulos ephasken zēn
verses.literal: vvv They only had some contentions with him regarding [their] own religion and - a certain Jesus [who] had died [but] whom - Paul affirmed to be alive

verses.original: δὲ ἐγὼ Ἀπορούμενος τὴν περὶ ζήτησιν τούτων ἔλεγον εἰ βούλοιτο πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα κἀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τούτων
verses.transliteration: de egō Aporoumenos tēn peri zētēsin toutōn elegon ei bouloito poreuesthai eis Hierosolyma kakei krinesthai peri toutōn
verses.literal: [Since] I was at a loss - as to how to investigate these [matters] I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried {there} on these [charges]

verses.original: δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἐπικαλεσαμένου αὐτὸν τηρηθῆναι εἰς τὴν διάγνωσιν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ ἐκέλευσα αὐτὸν τηρεῖσθαι ἕως οὗ ἀναπέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς Καίσαρα
verses.transliteration: de tou Paulou epikalesamenou auton tērēthēnai eis tēn diagnōsin tou Sebastou ekeleusa auton tēreisthai heōs hou anapempsō auton pros Kaisara
verses.literal: But [when] - Paul appealed - to be held over for the decision of the Emperor I ordered that he be held until - I could send him to Caesar

verses.original: δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν Φῆστον Ἐβουλόμην καὶ ἀκοῦσαι τοῦ ἀνθρώπου αὐτὸς Αὔριον Ἀκούσῃ αὐτοῦ φησίν
verses.transliteration: de Agrippas pros ton Phēston Eboulomēn kai akousai tou anthrōpou autos Aurion Akousē autou phēsin
verses.literal: Then Agrippa [said] to - Festus I would like - to hear [this] man myself Tomorrow you will hear him Festus declared

verses.original: οὖν Τῇ ἐπαύριον τοῦ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῆς Βερνίκης ἐλθόντος μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας καὶ εἰσελθόντων εἰς τὸ ἀκροατήριον σύν τε χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς κατ’ ἐξοχὴν ἀνδράσιν τῆς πόλεως καὶ τοῦ Φήστου κελεύσαντος ὁ Παῦλος ἤχθη
verses.transliteration: oun Tē epaurion tou Agrippa kai tēs Bernikēs elthontos meta pollēs phantasias kai eiselthontōn eis to akroatērion syn te chiliarchois kai tois kat’ exochēn andrasin tēs poleōs kai tou Phēstou keleusantos ho Paulos ēchthē
verses.literal: - The next day - Agrippa and - Bernice came with great pomp and entered . . . the auditorium along with - [the] commanders and - vvv leading men of the city And - Festus ordered that - Paul be brought in

verses.original: Καί ὁ Φῆστος φησιν βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄνδρες συμπαρόντες ἡμῖν θεωρεῖτε τοῦτον τὸ ἅπαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων πλῆθος ἐνέτυχόν μοι περὶ οὗ τε ἐνθάδε καὶ ἔν Ἱεροσολύμοις βοῶντες αὐτὸν δεῖν μὴ ζῆν μηκέτι
verses.transliteration: Kai ho Phēstos phēsin basileu Agrippa kai pantes hoi andres symparontes hēmin theōreite touton to hapan tōn Ioudaiōn plēthos enetychon moi peri hou te enthade kai en Hierosolymois boōntes auton dein mē zēn mēketi
verses.literal: Then - Festus said King Agrippa and all - [who] are present with us you see this [man] The whole vvv Jewish community has petitioned me about [him] both here and in Jerusalem crying out - [that] he ought not to live [any] longer

verses.original: δὲ ἐγὼ κατελαβόμην αὐτὸν πεπραχέναι μηδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου τούτου αὐτοῦ δὲ ἐπικαλεσαμένου τὸν Σεβαστὸν ἔκρινα πέμπειν
verses.transliteration: de egō katelabomēn auton peprachenai mēden axion thanatou toutou autou de epikalesamenou ton Sebaston ekrina pempein
verses.literal: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death [and] since he . . . vvv has now appealed to the Emperor I decided to send [him]

verses.original: ἔχω οὐκ τι ἀσφαλές γράψαι τῷ κυρίῳ περὶ οὗ διὸ προήγαγον αὐτὸν ἐφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ σοῦ βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα ὅπως ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης σχῶ τί γράψω τῆς
verses.transliteration: echō ouk ti asphales grapsai tō kyriō peri hou dio proēgagon auton eph’ hymōn kai malista epi sou basileu Agrippa hopōs anakriseōs genomenēs schō ti grapsō tēs
verses.literal: I have nothing . . . definite to write to [our] sovereign about [him] Therefore I have brought him before all of you and especially before you King Agrippa so that after this inquiry . . . I may have something to write -

verses.original: γάρ δοκεῖ ἄλογον μοι πέμποντα δέσμιον μὴ καὶ σημᾶναι τὰς αἰτίας κατ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: gar dokei alogon moi pemponta desmion mē kai sēmanai tas aitias kat’ autou
verses.literal: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without . . . specifying the charges against him
